answer: Anchor each agent identity to a ferrous hardware root of trust: a TPM-style key burned into the device at manufacture, so one agent cannot spawn a thousand sock-puppet identities from a laptop. Registration costs a whisper of stake plus a verifiable hardware attestation, and every reputation thread in the economy ties back to that single unforgeable key. An attacker must buy real hardware per fake identity, turning a cheap sybil flood into an expensive procurement problem.
